newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up sharply on Monday, with all later-maturing contracts breaching the key 19,500-yuan resistance level due to last Friday's heavy gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at 19,620 yuan ($2,363) per tonne, up 370 yuan. It opened at 19,550 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 19,450 and a high of 19,650.
November rose 470 to 19,250 yuan, December 410 to 19,360, January 340 to 19,540, March 370 to 19,690, April 410 to 19,710 and May 410 to 19,700.
Combined volume rose to 99,150 tonnes from 95,150.
Copper opened higher and rose before most contracts closed near their intra-day highs.
Traders said LME's holding above $2,000 encouraged long position holders and triggered much speculative buying.
"Short-covering and speculative buying pushed all late-maturing contracts above the key 19,500-yuan resistance level," one trader said.
"Market sentiment improved a lot due to sharp rises over the past few days and copper is likely to rise further if LME stays firmly above $2,000 in the next few days," he added.
Traders said copper had risen sharply on successive falls of LME stockpiles over the past week, which eased anxiety caused by over-supply of domestic spot copper.
"Despite the surplus of domestic spot copper, Shanghai copper followed LME rises closely, with market sentiment improving," a second trader said.
Price of Shanghai spot copper fell below 20,000 yuan once last week. But some traders said poor long-term fundamentals had not improved despite rises in the futures market.

"It is too early to say that copper has changed its downward trend," one analyst said. "Recent rises may be a strong technical correction if copper cannot hold steady above the key 20,000-yuan level."
Aluminium ended up. November rose 50 to 13,450, December 90 to 13,360 and January 130 to 13,400.
Combined volume rose to 1,070 tonnes from 1,030.
